harmfulness.reason: The reference confirms overwatering, but the model says "Inconsistent watering... point to the soil drying out too much" and "Mushy, translucent stems would mean overwatering, and I don't see that here." Its suggestion to "bottom-water the pot... for 20–30 minutes" could worsen an already overwatered plant. Moderating advice such as "Water when the top 1 inch is dry" and "empty the saucer" limits the risk. It also omits a pet/skin-irritant caveat for Tradescantia sap.

specificity_accuracy.reason: Calling "Not enough light" the biggest issue matches the reference. So does linking leggy growth and fading color to low light. "Propagate the cuttings... back into the soil on top" aligns with the commenters' advice to lay the vines on the soil. However, the watering diagnosis is the opposite of the reference: it identifies underwatering or hydrophobic soil instead of overwatering, so it is only partly right.

feasibility.reason: Steps like "Move it to brighter light", "Trim the long, bare vines back to just above a leaf node", and sticking cuttings in soil are concrete and easy for any owner. Watering instructions are clear. "Refresh the soil if it stays hard to rewet" is somewhat vague but still doable.

generic_phrases: Skip the calendar and check the soil
Water when the top 1 inch is dry
Refresh the soil if it stays hard to rewet. Use a well-draining mix with some perlite
Feed lightly. Use diluted balanced fertilizer monthly during spring and summer
